payload.title: Tue 11/24: Referring providers: weight loss medications and the behavioral half
payload.purpose: Patients on weight loss medications (never the drug class abbreviation): the habits that keep the result. Document post.

captions.LI:
Patients on weight loss medications often see dramatic physical results, but lasting change requires the behavioral half: the habits, coping skills, and relationship with food that keep the result after treatment.

The Bariatric Counseling Center provides group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one program. The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. Progress notes as requested. Call it two business days.

We accept most health insurances. Uniquely, the program is in-network with most health insurance plans, and patients typically attend for little to no cost.

Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales: lgonzales@bccsanantonio.com and 210-634-2200. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. payload.title: Thu 11/26: Lunch at the desk, again
payload.purpose: The workday eating pattern, without shame, and what dietary guidance in the program does with it.

captions.LI:
You're eating lunch at your desk again.

Not because you planned to. Not because it's the healthier choice. Because that's what the workday asked of you today.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our dietary guidance starts exactly there. Not with a meal plan that pretends your calendar is empty. With the calendar you actually have.

Our registered dietitians work with the rhythm of your real day. The meetings that run long. The commute. The desk lunch. We build nutritional strategies that fit the life you're living, not the one a textbook imagines.

That's part of what makes this program different. Dietary guidance that meets you where you are. Behavioral therapy that helps you understand your relationship with food. Cooking classes that make planning easier. Mindful movement that fits your schedule. One program, not four.

Serving clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas, the Bariatric Counseling Center offers an Intensive Outpatient Program designed for people who struggle with weight loss, binge eating, and chronic overeating. We're in network with most health insurance plans.

Learn more at bariatriccounselingcenter.com/program-schedule.

San Antonio and virtual across Texas
payload.alt_text: A desk lunch scene with the text 'Dietary guidance for your real day' overlaid.
payload.why_now: Posted on Thanksgiving week when many working professionals face disrupted eating schedules and feel guilt about desk meals during a holiday-shortened workweek.

payload.title: Tue 12/8: Referring providers: how a referral works
payload.purpose: Referral email intake@bccsanantonio.com, fax, NPI, Leloni Gonzales as Director of Admissions, call it two business days. Document post, last page repeats the contact.

captions.LI:
Referring a patient to the Bariatric Counseling Center takes two business days from submission to scheduled intake.

Providers can submit referrals by email to intake@bccsanantonio.com, by fax to 210-764-1129, or by calling our Director of Admissions, Leloni Gonzales, at 210-634-2200.

We ask for the patient's name, contact information, insurance details, and the referring provider's NPI number. Our team confirms insurance eligibility, contacts the patient directly, and schedules their first session.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medications that patients receive from their medical providers. We coordinate care with referring providers and provide progress notes as requested.

The Bariatric Counseling Center serves patients both onsite in San Antonio and virtual across Texas. We accept most health insurances, and our claims are processed under patients' mental health benefits.

Refer a patient at bariatriccounselingcenter.com/refer-a-patient/.

#BehavioralHealth
